# The Arts Across the Four Eras

How a society makes beauty follows from how it makes a living. The arts of this world
are read off its economy and its cognition ([[economy]], [[artifacts-and-memory]]): who
has time, who has materials, and what a made thing is *for*. Across the four eras
([[cycles]]) the same crafts — music, dance, weaving, pottery, glass, land-art — change
their meaning as the political weather changes.

## The requirement
> status: ratified (D-0091)

The arts are to be speculated across all four time periods — pre-history, the present,
the reconstruction era, and the narrator's present — spanning visual art, performing
art, music and dance, and craft (pottery, embroidery, glasswork). Each choice must be
motivated by what is already established as true of the world, and must stay coherent
with the economy and the broader social rules. Art here is never decoration bolted on;
it is a legible product of its era's material conditions.

## Pre-history — the arts of the commons
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch. In the pre-collapse commons, art and infrastructure are the same
act. Dance is applied topology: figures walked inside the stone circles are how a
community calculates its seasons together ([[megaliths-and-leys]]). Music is tuned to
ley-frequencies, resonance as a public utility. Loom-halls are where master weavers
encode continent-spanning treaties into cloth, and Wyrd-resonant pottery holds
"blessings" the way a vessel holds water. Chalk-hill land art is cut to be read from the
sky — addressed to the apex beasts, not to other people. The through-line: in a commons,
the made thing is shared cognition, not private property.

## The present — the bifurcation
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch. Under the empire the arts split in two. Imperial art is mass-produced
sterility: woodblock-stamped Ledgers, glasswork of merciless symmetry, iron worked dead
straight — every material forced to reject the organic curve, beauty as a demonstration
of control. Against it, proletariat craft goes underground and turns functional: proofs
embroidered into a hem, reckonings carved in bone and salvage, the protagonist's own
working deck painted on stolen scraped vellum in soot-and-bog-berry ink
([[artifacts-and-memory]]). Even grief is made useful — the keening becomes an atonal
acoustic tool for demolishing stagnant debt. This is the deskilling-versus-embodied-
knowledge fault line of the [[economy]] rendered as aesthetics.

## The reconstruction — mending as art
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch. In the rebuilding, the signature form is repair made visible:
kintsugi for the earth, where shattered imperial glass and broken ledgers are rebound
with sap and knot-work into communal tools that show their own history of breakage.
Pedagogy hides inside performance — detox-math taught as work-shanties, so a whole
valley reasons in chorus without knowing it is in school — and traveling theater troupes
move spoke to spoke, unlearning imperial habits through comedy. Art becomes the medium
of the endless rebuilding ([[cycles]]).

## The narrator's present — living monuments
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch. Centuries on, the arts are grown rather than built. Memorial groves
are cultivated into the shapes of historic proofs and bloom on the anniversary of their
making; the Great Braid, a continent-spanning continuous weaving, records history in a
strand each hub adds in turn. And there is the Silence — music composed of perfectly
timed rests, and clean wind heard for its own sake, because breathable air and quiet
were the luxuries the trio's generation bled to make possible. The remove is the point:
what the narrator's people take for granted is what the story's characters die for.
